chapterTitle: Chapter 4: Group V-A and Group VI-A Elements
title: Chapter 4: Group V-A and Group VI-A Elements
subject: chemistry-12

questions.question: In the industrial Haber-Bosch process for the synthesis of ammonia (N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃), the catalyst employed is:

options.A: Finely divided Iron (Fe) promoted with Al₂O₃ and K₂O

questions.explanation: Finely divided iron acts as catalyst while Al₂O₃ prevents sintering and K₂O acts as a promoter lowering activation energy.

questions.question: In the Ostwald process for the industrial manufacture of Nitric acid (HNO₃), the first step involves catalytic oxidation of ammonia over:

options.B: Platinum-Rhodium gauze at 800°C to form Nitric oxide (NO)

questions.explanation: 4 NH₃ + 5 O₂ xrightarrow{Pt-Rh, 800°C} 4 NO + 6 H₂O; NO is subsequently oxidized to NO₂ and absorbed in water.

questions.question: Aqua regia, capable of dissolving noble metals like gold and platinum, is a mixture of concentrated HCl and concentrated HNO₃ in the volume ratio of:
questions.explanation: Aqua regia is 3 parts concentrated HCl to 1 part concentrated HNO₃, producing nascent chlorine and nitrosyl chloride (NOCl).

questions.question: Which allotrope of phosphorus is translucent, waxy, highly toxic, and glows in the dark (chemiluminescence)?
questions.explanation: White phosphorus consists of strained P₄ tetrahedra, igniting spontaneously at 35°C and exhibiting chemiluminescent green glow.

questions.question: In the Contact Process for the manufacture of Sulfuric acid (H₂SO₄), the catalyst used for the oxidation of SO₂ to SO₃ is:
questions.explanation: V₂O₅ is the preferred industrial catalyst at 400°C-450°C because it is resistant to arsenic poisoning unlike platinum.

questions.question: Why is sulfur trioxide (SO₃) not absorbed directly into water in the Contact Process?

options.A: SO₃ is completely insoluble in water
options.B: The reaction is so violently exothermic that it produces a dense, unmanageable acid mist/fog that escapes condensation
options.C: It decomposes back to SO₂ and O₂

questions.explanation: Direct hydration creates a thick mist of fine H₂SO₄ droplets that will not condense easily; instead, SO₃ is absorbed in 98% H₂SO₄ to form oleum (H₂S₂O₇).

questions.question: What is the chemical name and formula of 'Oleum'?
questions.explanation: Absorption of SO₃ into concentrated H₂SO₄ yields H₂S₂O₇, known as oleum or fuming sulfuric acid.

questions.question: Which oxide of nitrogen is known as 'laughing gas' and used as a mild anesthetic?
questions.explanation: Nitrous oxide (N₂O) produces euphoria and hysterical laughter upon inhalation and is used in dental anesthesia.

questions.question: Nitrogen dioxide (NO₂) is a reddish-brown paramagnetic gas that readily dimerizes at lower temperatures to form a colorless, diamagnetic gas with formula:
questions.explanation: 2 NO₂ (brown, odd-electron paramagnet) ⇌ N₂O₄ (colorless, paired-electron diamagnet).

questions.question: What is the basicity (number of replaceable ionizable protons) of orthophosphoric acid (H₃PO₄)?
questions.explanation: H₃PO₄ has three -OH groups bonded to phosphorus: O=P(OH)₃; all three protons are ionizable, making it a tribasic acid.

questions.question: Phosphorous acid (H₃PO₃) acts as a reducing agent and is dibasic because its structure contains:

options.B: Two P-OH bonds and one direct non-ionizable P-H bond
options.C: One P-OH bond and two P-H bonds

questions.explanation: In H₃PO₃, phosphorus is bonded to one =O, two -OH groups, and one direct -H. The P-H hydrogen does not ionize but confers reducing power.

questions.question: Concentrated sulfuric acid acts as a powerful dehydrating agent. When it reacts with sucrose (cane sugar, C₁₂H₂₂O₁₁), the product is:

options.B: A spongy black mass of carbon (sugar charcoal) and steam

questions.explanation: C₁₂H₂₂O₁₁ xrightarrow{conc. H₂SO₄} 12 C + 11 H₂O; sulfuric acid removes the elements of water, leaving black spongy carbon.

questions.question: Which of the following compounds gives a positive brown ring test for the detection of nitrate (NO₃⁻) ions in qualitative analysis?
questions.explanation: The brown ring is nitroso ferrous sulfate complex: pentaaquanitrosyliron(II) sulfate [Fe(H₂O)₅(NO)]SO₄.

questions.question: Which allotrope of sulfur is thermodynamically stable at room temperature (below 95.6°C)?
questions.explanation: Rhombic (α) sulfur consisting of puckered S₈ rings is the most stable allotrope below the transition temperature of 95.6°C.

questions.question: What is the transition temperature at which rhombic sulfur and monoclinic sulfur coexist in equilibrium?
questions.explanation: At 95.6°C (transition point), rhombic and monoclinic sulfur have identical vapor pressures and coexist in dynamic equilibrium.

questions.question: Which reagent is used as an 'antichlor' in textile bleaching and as a 'fixer' in classic silver halide photography?
questions.explanation: Hypo dissolves unexposed silver halide: AgBr + 2Na₂S₂O₃ → Na₃[Ag(S₂O₃)₂] + NaBr, and destroys excess chlorine in bleached fabric.

questions.question: When concentrated nitric acid reacts with metallic copper, the dense brown gas evolved is:
questions.explanation: Cu + 4 HNO₃ (conc.) → Cu(NO₃)₂ + 2 NO₂ (red-brown gas) + 2 H₂O. Dilute HNO₃ gives colorless NO.

questions.question: White phosphorus is safely stored under which liquid in laboratories to prevent spontaneous ignition?
questions.explanation: White phosphorus is insoluble in and denser than water and does not react with water, cutting off atmospheric oxygen.

questions.question: The bleaching action of sulfur dioxide (SO₂) gas on colored materials is due to:
questions.explanation: SO₂ bleaches through temporary reduction; on standing in air, the reduced coloring matter is re-oxidized by atmospheric oxygen, restoring color.

questions.question: Ozone (O₃) acts as a powerful oxidizing agent because:

options.A: It readily decomposes to release one molecule of oxygen and one highly reactive nascent oxygen atom [O]
options.D: It has a cyclic triangular shape

questions.explanation: O₃ → O₂ + [O]. The liberated nascent oxygen atom has immense oxidizing potential (E° = +2.07 V).

questions.question: What is the geometry and bond angle of the ozone (O₃) molecule?
questions.explanation: The central oxygen is sp² hybridized with one lone pair and two bonding domains, producing a bent geometry with a bond angle of 116.8°.

questions.question: Which of the following elements in Group VA does not exhibit allotropy?
questions.explanation: Bismuth has only one metallic crystal structure and does not form allotropic modifications.

questions.question: Which of the following acids is known as the 'King of Chemicals' due to its ubiquitous use across all modern chemical industries?
questions.explanation: Sulfuric acid is produced in larger quantities than any other manufactured chemical, serving as a benchmark of a nation's industrial development.

questions.question: Why is dinitrogen (N₂) gas chemically inert at room temperature?

options.B: The nitrogen-nitrogen triple bond (N≡N) has an extraordinarily high bond dissociation energy (945 kJ/mol)

questions.explanation: The non-polar N≡N triple bond requires 945 kJ/mol to break, making N₂ unreactive under standard conditions.

questions.question: Which gas is evolved when concentrated sulfuric acid reacts with solid potassium iodide (KI)?

options.B: Purple iodine vapor (I₂) and sulfur dioxide (SO₂)

questions.explanation: Concentrated H₂SO₄ oxidizes the strong reducing agent HI into purple I₂ vapor while being reduced to SO₂ and H₂S.

questions.question: What is the oxidation state of sulfur in Caro's acid (peroxomonosulfuric acid, H₂SO₅)?
questions.explanation: H₂SO₅ has a peroxide bridge (-O-O- where O is -1 each) and three normal oxide oxygens (-2 each); sulfur is at its maximum +6 oxidation state.

questions.question: What gas turns acidified potassium dichromate (K₂Cr₂O₇) paper from orange to green?
questions.explanation: SO₂ reduces orange Cr₂O₇²⁻ (Cr⁺⁶) to green Cr³⁺ sulfate [Cr₂(SO₄)₃].

questions.question: Phosphine (PH₃) gas smells characteristically of:
questions.explanation: Phosphine has an unmistakable foul odor reminiscent of rotting fish or crushed garlic.

questions.question: Which of the following hydride molecules has the lowest bond angle due to the absence of significant hybridization (Drago's rule)?
questions.explanation: According to Drago's rule, in H₂S the bonds are formed using pure p-orbitals (~90°), resulting in an observed bond angle of ~92°.

questions.question: When sulfur is boiled with an aqueous solution of sodium sulfite (Na₂SO₃), the product formed is:
questions.explanation: Na₂SO₃ + S xrightarrow{\Delta} Na₂S₂O₃ (sodium thiosulfate).

questions.question: The tailing of mercury upon exposure to ozone is due to the formation of:
questions.explanation: 2 Hg + O₃ → Hg₂O + O₂. Dissolved Hg₂O causes mercury to lose its meniscus and stick (tail) to glass.

questions.question: Which acid is produced when P₄O₁₀ (phosphorus pentoxide) reacts with an excess of cold water?
questions.explanation: P₄O₁₀ + 2 H₂O (cold) → 4 HPO₃ (metaphosphoric acid). With hot water it yields H₃PO₄.

questions.question: The thermal decomposition of ammonium nitrite (NH₄NO₂) yields which gas?
questions.explanation: NH₄NO₂ xrightarrow{\Delta} N₂↑ + 2 H₂O; this is a standard laboratory method for preparing pure nitrogen gas.

questions.question: In the lead chamber process, oxides of nitrogen act as:

options.B: A homogeneous catalyst carrying oxygen from air to SO₂

questions.explanation: NO and NO₂ act as gaseous homogeneous catalysts, transferring oxygen: 2 NO + O₂ → 2 NO₂; NO₂ + SO₂ → SO₃ + NO.

questions.question: Hydrogen sulfide (H₂S) gas turns moist lead acetate paper black due to the formation of:
questions.explanation: Pb(CH₃COO)₂ + H₂S → PbS (insoluble black precipitate) + 2 CH₃COOH.
